f05395.reason: Akka was given as a greylag goose. Lagerlöf never names her species and her text keeps the flock's 'vildgäss' apart from 'grågäss' (ch. X: the wild geese meet some greylags on a skerry; ch. XXXVI: Dunfin is 'den lilla grågåsen' among 'alla vildgässen'). In 1906 Swedish folk speech 'vildgås' meant chiefly the bean goose (SAOB, quoting Ericson 1906), and ornithologists identify the Lapland-breeding flock as (taiga) bean geese. Answer changed to bean goose / Saatgans / гуменник, source and entity updated, flagged contested.

a1079.reason: The body called Akka and her flock greylag geese (and claimed this explains why the domestic gander keeps up). Lagerlöf's text distinguishes the wild geese from greylags (Dunfin is the greylag); the sentence now says the species is never named, that the flock is taken to be bean geese (the 1906 folk 'vildgås'), in EN/DE/RU; notes explain the accepted answer and the popular mistake.

a1163.reason: The body said a community garden is cultivated jointly 'rather than divided into private allotments'; many community gardens are in fact divided into individual plots (Wikipedia: 'Normally in community gardens, the land is divided into individual plots'). The sentence now says it may be one shared garden or individual beds, run together and open to the neighbourhood, in EN/DE/RU.

a1175.reason: The beech's share in the 2022 Bundeswaldinventur was given as about 16 per cent; the official results give 17 per cent (1.82 million ha = 16.6 per cent of the timberland), against 12 per cent for oak, so it remains the commonest broadleaved tree. Figure corrected in EN/DE/RU.

w05154.reason: The question stated as fact that the weever is the most venomous fish in Europe; reference sources rank it only as the most dangerous of the European weevers / among Europe's most dangerous venomous animals (FishBase, de.wikipedia). The wording now says it is 'regarded as' Europe's most venomous fish, matching the article's hedge, in EN/DE/RU.
